content:
I'm continuing to bridge the gaps in a definitional implementation of the deep inelastic scattering literature and the support in mathlib and physlib. This is leading me to some gaps in mathlib, e.g. no SU(N) Lie algebra, and some things that are defined in physlib that could also have gone into mathlib (Pauli matrices). Where is the boundary?

I'm in particular looking at:

  • Should Pauli matrices go up into mathlib? What about Gell-Mann matrices for SU(3)?
  • Should mathlib add SU(N) Lie algebras or does it make sense to stage this in physlib? They are a special form of the SL(N,C), so I don't think mathlib will want to just add a name for a special case that's then primarily used in a physics.
  • Where do we define the Casimirs? Mathlib has killingForm and traceForm, but in physics we talk about this in terms of Casimirs.
  • Finally, I'm looking to get to the generators of SU(N), as the thing that's relevant for the downstream physics.

I think the overarching philosophy in this direction is:

  1. If a result is in Mathlib we will not redefine it in Physlib. Really what goes into Mathlib is up to the community there, so below is some guesses.
  2. Though we might create an abbreviation of it with a more physics appropriate name (the 'physics context"), and might add specific lemmas which make them easier to use for physicists.
  3. If we think something is appropriate for Mathlib, it is ok to put it in Physlib now, and upstream later. Mathlib is often slower then Physlib at getting things in, so this should not hold us back.
  • For the Gell-Mann matrices, I struggle to see these getting into Mathlib anytime soon, so would make sense to keep them in Physlib (we actually already have them). Same with the Pauli matrices, although these probably have a higher likelihood.
  • For SU(N) this almost certainly will end up in mathlib, and then we would likely need an abbreviation.
  • For Casimirs, this falls under 2 now I think. I.e. we would give them a physics appropriate name in Physlib.

We have some of these things in: #Physlib > Project: Formalising the Yukawa sector of the Standard Model namely the Lie algebra of su(N) and the Gell-Mann matrices.

I think generally, there is no harm starting things in Physlib, since they are often done in the 'physicists way' and even if they appear in Mathlib, a lot of the results needed are physics specific, and would need proving/defining anyway

To add to the point above, sometimes adding something to mathlib with the express purpose of using it in physlib might not serve the purposes of mathilb or physlib. One of (the many) aims of mathlib is to be extremely optimized for downstream use, and as such, have the most general arguments possible and some style criteria that you would end up taking a long time iterating to get to. Although this is absolutely necessary in mathlib, it might not be needed for the purposes of physlib; so as joseph said above, getting a narrow construction into physlib to use for the physics purpose and refactoring later might be the way to go.

We have many such examples in physlib/mathematics, one that comes to mind is how there was constructions of the psuedo-remannian manifold, which served the immediate purpose and now should be refactored as mathlib has support for remannian geometry.
Thanks. I am behind on keeping up with the Yukawa sector thread :-( Still 1000 unread messages to read (about a month and a half, and the su(3) fields are just starting to appear)...
Yeah - obviously no expectation to read all those messages :). Just that if these are something you are also needing now, we can coordinate getting them into Physlib sooner in the best way possible.
